vision: An electronic batch record and logbook system for a GMP plant: the same web application on shop-floor tablets and office computers, always online, on the factory's own server, with no limit on users. R1 makes it trustworthy and delivers the logbooks and recipe design, R2 runs and releases batches, R3 proves capacity, links to the LIMS and delivers it on site.

releases.name: R1 Foundation and logbooks
releases.goal: A trustworthy platform (accounts, audit trail, signatures) that runs the same on tablet and desktop, the equipment logbooks, and the design and approval of master batch records.

tracks.summary: Runs alone first: skeleton, migration runner, route registry as a directory, test harness on a real database. Also owns the CI workflow of ebr (../.github/workflows/ebr.yml, outside this folder: named here because ownsFiles is relative to ebr/).

Local accounts with scrypt, database sessions, roles and permissions, TOTP, lockout. Writes its audit entries through server/audit (so it follows r1-audit-esign); provides the password check that e-signatures use (injected, so r1-audit-esign does not depend on it).
Audit trail in the same transaction with a hash chain; signatures with meaning and record version.
Touch-first shell and UI primitives; screens are found by directory (client/screens/<name>/), so later tracks add folders, not lines.
Logbooks driven by types the users create (fields, limits, signatures; versioned, QA-approved); equipment and rooms are built-in types; signed entries; status derived from the entries.
Master batch record designer, versions and QA approval.

releases.name: R2 Batch execution and release
releases.goal: Run batches on the shop floor from approved recipes, with limits, materials, equipment interlocks, review by exception and release.

tracks.summary: Batch from an effective MBR version, ordered steps, limits and exceptions; step types are files under server/steps/.
Released, unexpired lots by barcode or typing; weights with tolerance; yield and reconciliation.

Equipment status checked at the step; use entries written into the logbook automatically. Carries the engine extension both step groups need (effects after the signature, hooks at batch completion) as a gate patch to r2-execution's files.
Review by exception, disposition and the certified-copy PDF.

releases.name: R3 Scale, integration and delivery
releases.goal: Proven capacity for many users, directory sign-on, the LIMS link, on-premises installation, and the validation package.

tracks.summary: Load test with numbers, two instances behind a proxy.
LDAP/AD sign-on with group-to-role mapping and break-glass accounts.
Sample requests to the LIMS and results back, idempotent.
Docker images and Compose, Windows service, tested backup and restore.
The validation package generated from requirements and executed evidence (kit: assets/kits/validation).

releases.name: R4 Hardening
releases.goal: Close what the R1 to R3 package left open and that needs no decision from the plant: every character in certified copies, recipe copy, the Windows service proven, the harness proven.

tracks.summary: PDF writer with an embedded Unicode font, Arabic shaping and right-to-left order.
Copy a master version into a new draft master, audited, source recorded.
The service script exercised on a Windows Server runner: install, migrate, sign in, restart, uninstall.
Proof that the suite fails, never skips, without PostgreSQL.

gaps.title: Project skeleton, migration runner and test harness
acceptance: `npm test` runs unit and API tests against a fresh PostgreSQL database created per run, and fails when PostgreSQL is not reachable instead of skipping
Migrations are forward-only: applying them twice changes nothing, and a migration file edited after it was applied is refused at start-up
A route added as a new file under server/routes/ is mounted without editing a shared list (route table snapshot test)
A CI workflow runs the lint and the tests of ebr/ on every push that touches ebr/, against a PostgreSQL service

gaps.title: Accounts, sessions, roles and second factor
acceptance: A wrong password is refused and five failures in 15 minutes lock the account; the lock and each failure are in the audit trail
Sessions are stored in the database: two API instances on one database accept the same session, and a session revoked on one is refused by the other
Every route declares a permission; a route without one fails the route-table test, and a user without the permission gets 403
TOTP is required for roles flagged as privileged (QA, administrator)

gaps.title: Audit trail
acceptance: Every create and update writes its audit entry in the same transaction: a failure injected after the change leaves neither the change nor the entry
Audit entries carry user, server time (UTC), old and new value and reason; the API offers no update or delete of an entry, and a database role used by the application cannot update or delete them
The hash chain verifies; altering one stored entry makes verification report that entry

gaps.title: Electronic signatures
acceptance: A signature records signer, meaning, server time and the record version; the password is re-entered at signing and a wrong one is refused and audited
A record changed after signing shows the signature as invalid
The verifier of a step cannot be its performer: the server refuses it even if the client allows it

gaps.title: Touch-first shell for tablet and desktop
acceptance: The shell, sign-in and navigation pass Playwright tests at 820x1180 (tablet) and 1440x900 (desktop), with no horizontal scroll
Every interactive element is at least 44x44 px and reachable by keyboard; the accessibility lint has no error
The app is installable (manifest and service worker) but records nothing offline: with the network off, a save shows an error and nothing is stored locally

gaps.title: Equipment and rooms master data and logbook entries
acceptance: Equipment and rooms are created, changed and retired (never deleted) with audit entries

A logbook entry (use, cleaning, maintenance, calibration, status change) is signed by its author and cannot be changed afterwards; a correction is a new entry that references the old one with a reason
The logbook of one item lists its entries in time order with signer and meaning, and exports as a signed PDF

gaps.title: Equipment status engine
acceptance: Status (clean, dirty, in use, on hold, out of calibration) is derived from the logbook entries, not stored by hand
Clean hold time and calibration due date are configurable per item; when either passes, the status turns to dirty or out of calibration without anyone acting
A status change by hand needs a reason and a signature

gaps.title: Master batch record designer
acceptance: An MBR is built from phases and steps of the types instruction, data entry with limits, signature, verified step, calculation, material, equipment and sample
Limits, units and the order of steps are validated when the MBR is saved; an MBR with a calculation that refers to a missing step is refused
The designer works on a tablet and on a desktop (Playwright at both viewports)

gaps.title: MBR versions and approval
acceptance: An MBR version moves draft to in review to approved to effective; approval needs a QA signature from someone other than the author
Only one version of an MBR is effective at a time; making a new one effective retires the previous one
An approved version cannot be edited; a change creates a new draft version with the history kept

gaps.title: Batch creation and step execution
acceptance: A batch can be created only from an effective MBR version, and keeps a reference to that exact version
Steps run in the order the MBR defines; the server refuses a step out of order or a step whose phase is not started
Each recorded value is stored with performer, server time and the version read; a second tablet writing the same step with a stale version gets 409

gaps.title: Limits and exceptions during execution
acceptance: A value outside its limits is recorded, flagged as an exception at once and requires a comment; the batch cannot be closed while an exception is open
An exception can be raised as a deviation with its number, and the link is kept on the batch record
Calculated values are computed on the server from recorded values; the client cannot send them

gaps.title: Materials: dispensing, lot verification and reconciliation
acceptance: A material step accepts a lot only when it is released and not expired; the lot is read by typing or by the tablet camera scanning its barcode
Weights are checked against target and tolerance; an out-of-tolerance weight is an exception
Yield and material reconciliation are calculated at the end of the batch and differences beyond limits are exceptions

gaps.title: Equipment interlock and automatic logbook entries
acceptance: A batch step that uses equipment is refused when the equipment status is not clean or is out of calibration, with the reason shown
Starting and ending use in a batch writes the use entries into the equipment logbook automatically, with the batch number
Releasing the equipment after the batch sets it to dirty

gaps.title: Review by exception
acceptance: The review screen lists every exception, correction and late entry of a batch, and nothing else unless asked
QA cannot complete the review while an exception has no comment or open deviation link
Every review action is audited and signed with meaning reviewed

gaps.title: Batch disposition and certified copy
acceptance: Release or reject needs a QA signature and is refused while the review is not complete
The batch record exports as a PDF certified copy with all values, signatures, exceptions and the audit trail, generated from the stored record
The PDF carries a hash that the system can verify later

gaps.title: Capacity for an unlimited number of users
acceptance: A load test with 300 simulated users (each one signing in, opening batches and recording steps) holds p95 below 500 ms on the reference server, with zero failed writes
Two API instances behind a reverse proxy share load and sessions; stopping one does not lose a recorded step
No component counts users or enforces a user limit

gaps.title: Directory sign-on (LDAP/AD)
acceptance: Users can sign in with their directory account; roles are mapped from directory groups
When the directory is not reachable, sign-in fails with a clear message and local break-glass accounts still work

gaps.title: Link to the LIMS
acceptance: A sample step of a batch creates a sample request in the LIMS through its API, and the LIMS result is shown on the batch when it is approved there
When the LIMS is down the step shows the failure and can be retried without creating the request twice

gaps.title: On-premises delivery
acceptance: `docker compose up` on a clean server starts the application and PostgreSQL with migrations applied and a first administrator created
The Windows service installer runs the same build on a Windows Server without Docker
Backup and restore are tested: a restored backup passes the audit chain verification

gaps.title: Validation package
acceptance: URS, FRS, risk assessment, RTM, IQ, OQ and the summary report are generated from the requirements and executed tests; nothing is typed as a result
Every Critical or High requirement links to a passed executed test or an open deviation

gaps.title: Create any logbook: configurable logbook types
acceptance: A user with the permission can create a new logbook type (for example balance, temperature, room cleaning, utility, instrument) with its own fields: text, number with unit and limits, date and time, choice list, yes/no, signature with meaning
A logbook type is versioned and is used only after a QA signature by someone other than its author; changing it creates a new version, and entries keep the version they were written with
Logbooks are created from an approved type for any object (equipment, room, area, instrument, process) without a code change; equipment and room logbooks are built-in types made the same way
An entry is validated on the server against its type version: unknown fields are refused, a number outside its limits is flagged at once and needs a comment

gaps.title: Every character in exports and certified copies
acceptance: The logbook PDF and the batch certified copy print any text of the record, Arabic (joined letters, right to left) and accented Latin included; no character is replaced or dropped

For an Arabic, an English and a mixed line: the text the PDF carries for the line (what a reader copies and searches) equals the stored text, and an independent PDF reader finds every one of its characters
A certified copy made before this change still verifies against its registered hash

gaps.title: Copy a recipe into a new master
acceptance: A user with the MBR design permission copies any version of a master into a new master in draft; the copy carries the design and records the source master and version
The copy is audited, needs its own review and QA approval, and changes nothing in the source

gaps.title: Windows service installation proven on Windows Server
acceptance: On a Windows Server runner, install-service.ps1 installs the built application as a service against PostgreSQL 16; it migrates, answers health, and the first administrator signs in
Stopping the service and starting it again keeps the data; uninstalling removes the service and leaves the database

gaps.title: The test harness refuses to run without its database
acceptance: Running the suite with PostgreSQL unreachable fails with the reason and runs no test; nothing is skipped silently

droppedOrDeferred.idea: Offline recording on tablets with later sync
droppedOrDeferred.why: Decided by the user: always online. Offline signing would need its own QA decision and a much larger design.
Not chosen; the record is fully electronic.

droppedOrDeferred.idea: Integration with the LIMS from R1
droppedOrDeferred.why: Decided by the user: standalone first, link in R3.
